name: B10-0109/2026 – Motion for a resolution
title: MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the draft Commission implementing decision renewing the authorisation for the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of or produced from genetically modified cotton GHB614 × LLCotton25 pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 1829/2003 of the European Parliament and of the Council
part_text:
The European Parliament is asking the European Commission to withdraw its plan to renew the licence for a genetically modified cotton, called GHB614 × LLCotton25. This cotton is engineered to survive spraying with two weedkillers, glyphosate and glufosinate. The Parliament says the safety checks were incomplete, that glufosinate is banned in the European Union, and that the cotton would increase herbicide use. It also says the Commission should not approve genetically modified crops when member states have not backed them. This is the Parliament's opinion; it does not itself change the law.

- **What changes:** Nothing yet. The Parliament only asks the Commission to drop the renewal plan.
- **Who it affects:** Farmers, food and feed importers, and consumers in the European Union.
- **What happens next:** The Commission decides whether to withdraw its plan or keep it.
